Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait. Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist. We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx). Â The Opportunity Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own. We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live. We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range. You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture. What you'll do Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between. Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy. Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site. Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range. Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture. What we're looking for 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering. You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services. You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded. You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them. You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity. You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required. How we work We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. Weâre growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the role This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers â from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs. The day-to-day: Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts â new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts. Responsibilities Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management. Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity). Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means. Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly. Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs. Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns. Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures. Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals. What we're looking for Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up. title: Senior Software Engineer
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior, Manager. We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable. Our stack is Python ( FastAPI ) on AWS , with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows. Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD . What You Will Do: Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end. Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails. Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production. Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality. Drive the full software development lifecycle , translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans. What We Are Looking For: 5+ years building and operating production backend systems , with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end. Deep fluency in your primary backend language , and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python ; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly. Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one. Sound reasoning under ambiguity : you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change. Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations , including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar). Professional written English , enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs. Even Better: AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience. Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions. A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal. How We Hire: We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build: 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit.. 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review. You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment. What We Offer: Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package. Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work. The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI , tackling hard problems with high ownership. A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement. If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk! Originally posted on Himalayas

Monitor and optimize LLM token usage and costs across providers, maintain centralized cost tracking dashboards and alerting across business units, and recommend cost-efficient model routing and provider selection strategies. Develop production-grade services and tooling, primarily in Python, on Kubernetes, applying strong engineering practices (testing, code reviews, CI/CD, observability, security), and document standards, architecture diagrams, and operational playbooks for other teams. Strong GCP experience preferred, including hands-on work with GKE, BigQuery (data warehousing, SQL, schema management), Pub/Sub, Vertex AI (batch prediction, model deployment), Cloud SQL, GCS, and IAM. Experience building or operating ML infrastructure (feature stores, orchestration platforms, model serving, annotation tools) is highly desirable. Ability to communicate effectively with data scientists, ML engineers, and product stakeholders in both business and technical contexts. Comfort participating in an on-call rotation and working in a trustful, respectful, and collaborative environment. title: Technical Co-founder (CTO) - AI for Automotive Retail
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Executive. The Opportunity Every used-car dealer's profit is made or lost the moment they buy the car — not when they sell it. That decision runs on gut feel, spreadsheets, and whoever has a spare hour, inside a $500B+ industry that hasn't meaningfully modernized how it buys. We think that's an AI-native category waiting to be built, and we're going first. The problem and solution are validated with a domain co-founder who lives this daily and has already hand The Venture Atrium is an always-on AI workforce, not a dashboard — agents that watch, learn, and earn the right to act on their own, deployed inside dealer groups' existing workflows. The same decision logic has to show up everywhere the work already happens — web, desktop, our own browser, mobile — so the workforce follows the person, not the other way around. One brain, every surface. This isn't a weekend's worth of CRUD. Think dozens of specialist agents organized into a handful of coordinated workflows, sharing one memory, each one earning the right to act on its own track record — across four surfaces at once. If that sounds like a fun problem rather than a scary one, keep reading. A real technical moat if built right, and a wide-open field — no dominant AI-native player has claimed this category yet. Specifics on the product, the model, and where we stand commercially are best shared in conversation; we're early and staying deliberately quiet in the market. The Partnership CEO and domain co-founder are in place; the problem is validated. We're looking for a technical co-founder to own product and engineering from the first commit — full authority, founder equity, a real seat at the table on every major call. This is a co-founder role, not a CTO hire. In return for that level of commitment, you receive founder-level equity, founder-level authority with co-decision rights on product, technology, hiring, fundraising, and strategy, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision. What you'll own As Co-Founder & CTO, you will take over the production code and continue building the product (the first lines of production code), set the technical direction, and lead execution end-to-end. Own the core architecture decision that shapes everything else — how the agents actually see and act in a dealer's world, and how one system stays coherent across a web app, a desktop app, our own browser, and mobile, without four separate products drifting apart Design the autonomy model: how an agent earns the right to act alone, and how that trust is never assumed Build the integration layer into a data ecosystem that won't always cooperate Build partnerships with ecosystem data providers and third-party systems to land unconventional integrations no standard API gets you Own unit economics as an architecture problem, not an afterthought — this many agents, across this many surfaces, has to add up Own the design and layering of the system for the dev team, and keep the build matched to what the business and sales side actually need Be the technical voice with dealers, design partners, and investors Hire and lead the founding engineering team Co-Founder Profile Must Have: Has shipped agentic or LLM systems into production where being wrong actually costs something Has shipped desktop and mobile apps connected to a larger web platform — comfortable with one product living across multiple facets and surfaces, not just a single app Has shipped LLM-based products, but also worked with SLMs and SLM fine-tuning Has dealt with the real nuances of web scraping — anti-bot defences, rate limits, brittle DOMs, the gap between "works in a demo" and "works at scale against a site that doesn't want you there" Has built complex, modelled data graph layers for intelligence — not just a data pipeline, but a structure that reasoning can actually run on Comfortable owning infra, data, and product alone — then hiring past yourself Treats guardrails and reversibility as core product, not overhead Good to have: edge computing and power-constrained systems, high-frequency distributed computing infrastructure Great to Have: Experience building against locked-down or adversarial third-party data Vertical/operational domain grit (Automotive) Pragmatic and creative — a solution finder who gets to "working" fast and iterates from there Co-operative, strategic, and hands-on in equal measure How to Apply Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate. FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences. Originally posted on Himalayas

This role is focused on investigating and responding to security incidents and threat attempts to protect our cloud-based environment. YOUR IMPACT Lead the hands-on investigation, triage, and response to security incidents and threat attempts, directly protecting our cloud-based environment; Drive the development and execution of cybersecurity projects and mitigation plans in close collaboration with IT, Cloud Security, and engineering teams; Actively enhance our cybersecurity observability, refining tools and processes to detect and counter internal and external threats more effectively; Serve as a first line responder during incident response activities, ensuring rapid triage, containment, and timely communication to all relevant stakeholders; Help build and maintain customer trust by contributing directly to the creation and delivery of safe, secure, and resilient products; Organize and manage interdependencies between security initiatives and other technology areas to ensure cohesive, comprehensive protection for the entire ecosystem; Develop, update, and maintain automations to accelerate security ticket triage and enhance the efficiency of incident response workflows; Design, evaluate, and operate AI-assisted workflows (LLMs and agents) for alert triage, enrichment, and incident response, with human-in-the-loop controls; Contribute to detection and response coverage for AI-related risks, including LLM applications, AI agents, and employee use of AI tools; Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Requirements About the Role We're looking for an AI Engineer to help build the next generation of AI-powered enterprise solutions. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, QA, and AI leadership to ensure every solution delivers real business value while meeting enterprise standards for security, performance, and governance. Beyond technical delivery, you'll bring product thinking and commercial awareness, helping to identify meaningful customer challenges, emerging AI opportunities, and relevant market trends. Your insights will contribute to shaping and refining the Agent Factory roadmap and backlog. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building practical AI applications and can take solutions from concept through to production deployment. What You'll Be Doing Build and Deliver Intelligent Agents Design, build and deploy AI agents that solve real customer and business problems. Create agents that deliver value independently while contributing insights to a broader intelligence ecosystem. Translate product requirements and use cases into scalable, production-ready solutions. Develop MCP-Based Integrations Build and operate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that provide agents with secure access to tools, systems and enterprise data. Define and implement tool interfaces, authentication mechanisms and resource access patterns. Ensure agents can interact with enterprise services in a structured, secure and reliable way. Integrate Enterprise Systems Connect agents with business-critical platforms including: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Microsoft Graph Dataverse ServiceNow Contact Centre and Customer Experience platforms Internal and third-party APIs Design Context, Memory & Intelligence Define how agents manage memory, context and decision-making patterns. Implement retrieval, reasoning and tool-use strategies that promote consistent and predictable behaviour. Design guardrails that enable agents to operate safely and effectively within enterprise environments. Contribute to the Agent Ecosystem Develop supporting services including adapters, event processing capabilities and integration layers. Enable agents to share insights and consume intelligence from a wider ecosystem of interconnected solutions. Help shape future product direction by contributing technical expertise, customer insights and market observations. What You'll Bring Microsoft Technology Expertise Strong software engineering experience using C# and .NET . Hands-on experience with Azure services, including: Azure Functions Azure App Service Azure OpenAI Service Azure AI Foundry / AI Studio Experience integrating with Microsoft business platforms such as: Dynamics 365 Dataverse Microsoft Graph Power Platform Knowledge of Azure security and identity services, including: Microsoft Entra ID Managed Identities Azure Key Vault Agentic AI & MCP Experience Practical experience building or consuming MCP servers. Knowledge of agent frameworks and orchestration technologies such as: Semantic Kernel AutoGen Microsoft AI SDKs Experience with: Function and tool calling Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Vector databases Context and memory management Ability to design clear, reliable and secure agent interactions.# Broader Engineering Skills Strong API integration experience, including REST APIs, webhooks and event-driven architectures. Experience with cloud-native deployment, CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code approaches. Understanding of performance, latency, reliability and cost considerations when working with Large Language Models in production. Commitment to software quality, testing and continuous improvement. Ability to work closely with QA teams on agent evaluation, testing and quality assurance. Who You Are You'll be successful in this role if you are: A pragmatic builder who can take ideas from concept to production. Passionate about applying AI to solve real-world business challenges. Comfortable working independently while collaborating with cross-functional teams. A systems thinker who understands how individual components contribute to larger platforms and architectures. Security-conscious and focused on building reliable enterprise-grade solutions. Excited by emerging AI technologies and eager to learn as the landscape evolves. Nice to Have While not essential, we'd be particularly interested in candidates with experience in: Multi-agent architectures and agent-to-agent communication. Delivering AI solutions within enterprise or regulated environments. LLM observability, monitoring, tracing, and evaluation frameworks. Contact Centre, Customer Experience, or enterprise workflow automation platforms. Why Join Us? This is an opportunity to help shape the future of AI within a rapidly evolving product organisation. You'll work with cutting-edge Microsoft AI technologies, contribute directly to innovative agentic solutions, and play a key role in building scalable AI capabilities that deliver measurable value to customers. If you're passionate about building intelligent systems and want to be at the forefront of enterprise AI innovation, we'd love to hear from you. All employees are expected to actively support and maintain the organisation's information security standards and contribute to protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of company and customer information. This includes: Adhering to all applicable information security policies, procedures and guidelines at all times. Protecting company, customer and partner data from unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration or loss. Using company systems, devices and networks in a secure and compliant manner. Promptly reporting any suspected or actual security incidents, breaches or vulnerabilities to the appropriate team. Completing mandatory information security and data protection training as required. description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior. AI Technology Partners (AITP) is a leader in delivering cutting-edge generative AI solutions and managed services, specializing in secure, customizable AI deployments for enterprises. Our offerings are designed to help organizations unlock the full value of AI while maintaining robust security and compliance across their infrastructures. About the role At AI Technology Partners (AITP), we empower enterprises to scale revenue & profit —with secure, compliant generative AI solutions. In this role, you’ll lead the design and delivery of agentic systems that orchestrate tools, data, and policies to solve real business workflows—safely, reliably, and at scale. If you like greenfield architecture, fast iteration, and measurable impact with enterprise clients, this is your playground. What you'll do Architecture & System Design (Agentic) Design multi-agent architectures with robust state management, memory, and routing. Choose and implement leading frameworks such as LangGraph/LangChain Agents, Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex Agents, Semantic Kernel, or Haystack Agents—and justify trade-offs. Build modular components (planners, tool registries, policy guards, evaluators) that are reusable across clients and domains. Tooling & Orchestration Integrate enterprise tools and data sources via function/tool calling, webhooks, and event-driven flows (Queues/Service Bus/Functions). Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns with vector stores (Azure AI Search, pgvector, MongoDB Atlas, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus) and structured knowledge (SQL/Graph). Add deterministic fallbacks, circuit breakers, and caching to keep latency and cost predictable. Reliability, Observability & MLOps Define SLIs/SLOs for agent runs; implement tracing, metrics, and logging (e.g., Langfuse + OpenTelemetry) and build dashboards for run-level analytics. Create evaluation harnesses (automatic + human-in-the-loop) using tools such as Ragas, DeepEval, promptfoo to measure groundedness, task success, safety, and cost. Productionize with CI/CD, environment promotion, feature flags, and canary strategies; optimize cost-per-task and time-to-success. Safety, Security & Governance Enforce content and safety policies (redaction, classification, guardrails) with policy-as-code; implement role/tenant isolation and data minimization. Collaborate with security teams to align to ISO 27001/SOC 2/NIST/HIPAA/GDPR contexts; deliver audit-ready evidence for agentic workflows. Build privacy-first patterns (no data exfiltration by default, least-privilege tool access, secure prompt/trace storage). Product & Client Impact Work directly with enterprise client teams to translate business processes into agentic designs; present trade-offs and proofs-of-value that lead to production. Partner with solution leads to create domain-specific agents (e.g., RFP assist, incident RCA drafting, knowledge ops) and reusable templates. Qualifications Must-have 5–8+ years in software/platform engineering with recent production LLM applications (not just prototypes). Hands-on expertise with agentic frameworks (one or more of: LangGraph/LangChain Agents, AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex Agents, Semantic Kernel, Haystack Agents) and tool/function-calling patterns. Strong RAG engineering across vector DBs, chunking/embedding strategies, metadata/search ranking, and grounding techniques. Proven track record building observable, cost-aware, and secure LLM systems (tracing, evals, guardrails, secrets/IAM, PII handling). Solid software engineering fundamentals: Python/TypeScript, async patterns, APIs, testing, CI/CD, containerization. Clear communicator who can interface with clients and write crisp technical docs. Nice to have Azure-first experience (Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Studio, Azure Functions/Container Apps/AKS, Private Link/VNet, Key Vault, Entra ID). Cross-cloud exposure (AWS/GCP) and hybrid integrations; experience with enterprise connectors (SharePoint/OneDrive, ServiceNow, Salesforce). Experience with structured output, constrained decoding, JSON Schemas, and program-of-thought planning. Location Remote, US-based candidates preferred. The role may involve working across multiple time zones. How we work Ownership & velocity: Small team, big surface area. You’ll design, ship, and iterate quickly. Security by design: Data governance and safety are table stakes, not afterthoughts. Evidence over vibes: We measure task success, grounding, and cost—and improve with data. AI as leverage: We use LLMs to accelerate engineering—not replace it. Compensation We offer a competitive and flexible compensation package aligned to experience, scope, and engagement model. This may include base salary, performance incentives, and equity participation, designed to reward meaningful contributions and impact. What we offer Challenging work on meaningful, production agentic systems for enterprise clients. Learning & sharing culture with deep dives, brown bags, and support for certifications/publication. Inclusive, flexible workplace —bring your whole self; work where you do your best thinking. How to Apply Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their resumes and a brief cover letter outlining relevant experience and why they are a good fit for this role. Equal Opportunity Statement AI Technology Partners is committed to equal employment opportunity in all practices and reaffirms that there shall be no unlawful discrimination against any employee or applicant for employment on the grounds of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Executive. The studio's work spans wherever a market and the data or infrastructure underneath it are broken enough to justify building the fix from scratch. About The General Data Corporation General Data is the infrastructure for licensing proprietary data: The platform runs the whole deal from request to delivery, with privacy checks, rights evidence and contracts built in. The vision is to become the system of record between AI and the world’s private data, the data that has never been published but that the next generation of AI depends on. On one side are enterprises, AI labs and robotics teams that need real-world data, and on the other are companies whose operations generate it. General Data is the data infrastructure for the modern economy, connecting every party so that data can be licensed safely, transparently and at scale. Why this is a unique opportunity AI has absorbed the public internet, and its next gains will come from private, real-world data, yet today these deals still run on email, WhatsApp and brokers, with no visibility into what was checked, who holds the rights, or whether personal data was removed. Labs are already paying for this data, and regulation like GDPR and the EU Data Act makes a trusted, verifiable layer a necessity. General Data is VC-backed and looking for its technical co-founder. Together with Founder & CEO Louai Allani, you will own the product and architecture, shape the company’s direction as an equal partner and build the team from the ground up. About the role Supplier intake: Build connectors for where companies actually keep their data: Databases, document stores, ticketing systems, machine logs, and sensor and video archives. Transaction layer: Own the pipeline, rights evidence, contracts, permissions, audit trail and delivery API. ML and data quality: Build anonymisation across text, tables, images and video, plus re-identification checks, deduplication, quality scoring and tooling that turns raw records into training-ready data. Delivery and compute: Decide whether data is processed in our cloud or inside the supplier’s environment. Build secure delivery, recurring updates and our GPU infrastructure. Technical direction: Own the architecture and roadmap. Work directly with labs, suppliers and researchers to understand what the system needs to become. What you need to succeed Data infrastructure at scale: You have built pipelines for large unstructured datasets, such as video, images, sensor logs or documents, at terabyte scale or more. Physical-world data: You have worked with documents, logs, video or sensor streams, ideally in robotics, industrial or autonomous systems and know what embodied AI teams need from data and where it breaks. Sensitive data: You know how to handle personal and confidential data safely. Experience with regulated data is a plus. Technical leadership: You make architectural decisions, explain them clearly and raise the engineering bar as the team grows. Hands-on Builder: You have taken a product, platform or open-source project from 0 to 1 that others relied on, and you still write code and own the critical paths. Founder mindset: You care about the outcome, not the title. You form strong views, test them quickly and are comfortable owning technical, product and operational problems. Location: Paris preferred. English required; French is a plus. Please note: As a co-founder, you take a real stake in what we build. The compensation is a founder salary, and your upside grows with the company through your equity. Come build the infrastructure between AI and the world's data with us! Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Staff Network Engineer (AI Infrastructure)
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior. As a Staff Network Engineer at vCluster Labs , you aren't just configuring switches; you are building the automation logic that configures them. AI Clouds run on InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics that most teams still wire up by hand, one customer at a time. You will build the automation that turns that fabric into repeatable provisioning logic. You start in a small R&D group alongside our CTO and grow into owning this area as it becomes a core part of our platform. As a Staff Network Engineer, your role will include: Fabric automation: You will design and build the systems that automatically provision and configure NVIDIA switches and InfiniBand fabrics, including integration with NVIDIA UFM. Manual, per-customer switch setup is the thing you are replacing. Network config management and sync: You will build the control loop that keeps switch, VLAN, and VXLAN state consistent with what our platform intends, detects drift, and reconciles it safely in production. NAT gateway and L4 load balancing: You will build the gateway and load balancing layer that tenant clusters depend on for connectivity, with failover designed in from day one rather than bolted on later. Scale and failure engineering: You will define how our network layer behaves at large scale: BGP route table limits, convergence, failover, and what happens when a link, switch, or gateway dies under real AI workloads. Customer Zero for AI networking: You will run your automation on real AI Cloud environments, bring back what breaks, and turn hard-won operational lessons into product behavior our customers never have to think about. Technical direction: You will help decide what we build versus integrate with partner solutions, write the design and requirements docs, and set the standards for how networking works across vCluster products. This role could be a fit for you if you bring: You have built network automation, not just operated networks: You have shipped software that configures switches, routers, or load balancers programmatically, ideally as part of a product or internal platform other teams relied on. NVIDIA networking experience: Hands-on work with NVIDIA UFM, NVIDIA Spectrum or Quantum switches, Cumulus Linux, or NVUE, including programming against their APIs. Deep fabric fundamentals: Strong command of InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, including how they behave and fail at production scale. Production scale scars: You have run networks at real production scale, seen them break, and helped fix the root cause with automation rather than runbooks. Software engineering ability: You write production code in Go or Python, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and think of network config as code. Bonus points for: AI networking depth: Experience tuning fabrics for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, congestion control, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X. AI Cloud or hyperscaler background: You helped build network automation at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, or large CDN. Load balancer and gateway internals: Experience building L4 load balancers or NAT gateways, including with eBPF/XDP or DPDK. Open source: Contributions to networking or Kubernetes projects such as SONiC, FRRouting, Cilium, or MetalLB. About vCluster Labs We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture. We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software. We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems. Premium Insurance : Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country). Define the secure coding standards and reference patterns that teams across the enterprise build against. Build the vulnerability prioritization capability that shows where real risk sits across code, pipelines, and deployed services, and drive remediation to measurable closure. Establish a threat modeling practice for applications, APIs, and delivery pipelines that scale beyond a single team. CI/CD & software supply chain security Architect the security control layer for our CI/CD platforms (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab, Azure DevOps) so every pipeline inherits it by default. Design the automated testing pipeline that runs SAST, DAST, SCA, and container scanning on every build, tuned for signal over noise. Build the automation that keeps our attack surface visible: API discovery, dependency scanning, SBOM generation, and secrets detection. AI/LLM security & AI-powered automation Build reusable AI agent skills and workflows inside CI/CD (e.g., agentic coding tools, MCP-based integrations) that review every pull request for insecure patterns, authN/authZ gaps, secrets exposure, and risky dependency changes, and deliver CWE/OWASP-mapped findings developers can act on. Build AI-driven security testing that generates targeted test cases (API abuse cases, fuzzing inputs, prompt-injection and jailbreak suites), triages SAST/SCA/DAST results to cut false positives and proposes remediation PRs for human review. Define the guardrails AI agents operate under our pipelines: least-privilege tokens, human-in-the-loop approval, output-accuracy evaluation, and audit logging. title: AI Architect
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior. Principal Data Scientist, AI (Architect-Level Scope) About KLDiscovery KLDiscovery is a global eDiscovery and legal technology provider serving large law firms, corporate legal departments, and government agencies. We build and operate the products and services that legal teams rely on to manage, process, and review case data at scale. With operations across multiple countries and a client base that includes AmLaw 200 firms, we handle some of the largest and most complex matters in the industry. About the Role We're hiring our most senior AI practitioner — someone with genuine data science rigor who also wants to build. In this role, you'll set the scientific and architectural direction for gen AI and ML at KLDiscovery : designing the evaluation methodology that proves our AI holds up under legal scrutiny, choosing and validating the models and retrieval systems that power our products, and building the hardest parts of that system yourself. This is one of the most interesting data science problem sets in enterprise software. You'll work with terabytes of real-world legal data — emails, contracts, chat transcripts, images, video, depositions, and regulatory filings — from some of the largest litigation and investigation matters in the world. The work is hard in ways that matter: documents are messy and adversarial, the stakes are real (privilege, defensibility, attorney work product), and getting the evaluation wrong has real consequences. AI that can surface key people, themes, and timelines in hours instead of weeks, or pre-classify millions of documents for relevance and privilege with results that survive scrutiny, directly changes the economics of how legal matters get resolved. We build solutions that turn data into evidence the legal system can trust. This is a builder-first role, not a research-only or advisory one. You'll design experiments and evaluation frameworks that prove our AI is defensible in court, build the retrieval and agent systems that reason over case data, and personally ship the hardest, most novel parts of that system. You'll set strategic direction across Nebula, our eDiscovery platform, and CS & Operations, then prove out the science and the architecture by building it yourself. Not a role for anyone stepping back from the keyboard, and not a role for anyone who treats evaluation as an afterthought. We offer competitive total compensation that includes base pay, bonus potential, equity, inclusive benefits, wellness programs, and perks. We use market and industry data to inform pay decisions while considering geography and labor markets, individual experience, and business needs. Individual compensation will vary, although a reasonable estimate of the current annualized base pay range for this position is $190,000 to $240,000. Job location: Remote (candidate must be based in the United States) Key Responsibilities Own the science and the architecture, and build both personally. Design the experimentation and evaluation methodology that determines whether our AI's outputs are accurate, consistent, and defensible — then define the end-to-end gen AI architecture across Nebula and CS & Operations to deliver on it: LLMs, agent harnesses, RAG, vector search, embeddings, and model selection and triage. Build the hardest parts personally: prototype agent loops, design and run the evaluations that validate them, tune retrieval, and ship the shared infrastructure that powers AI Case Explorer (case overviews, timelines, key people and themes, PII surfacing, and Agent chat), AI Agent Review (pre-classifying relevance, privilege, and key issues, shipping MLP), and CS & Ops tech-enablement as part of our central work orchestration system. Own evaluation rigor, AI/MLOps, and telemetry end-to-end. Design the statistical and experimental methodology behind our evaluation harnesses — the standard our outputs have to meet to hold up under legal scrutiny — and own the infrastructure that enforces it: model deployment and versioning, eval pipelines, drift and quality monitoring, cost and latency telemetry, and prompt and agent observability. Define and implement how we select, triage, and route across models (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source, fine-tuned), manage vector databases and retrieval, and evolve our evaluation methodology and agent harness as the frontier moves. Lead the practice from the front. Set the technical and scientific bar by building, not by reviewing. Partner with Engineering, Product, and Data Science leadership to translate that rigor into shipped product. Raise the bar on both AI engineering and evaluation discipline, mentor senior ICs through hands-on technical leadership, build and maintain relationships with model and infrastructure vendors, and represent KLD's AI strategy directly with customers, partners, and at industry events. What You Bring (Required) 7+ years in data science, applied AI/ML, or ML engineering, with recent hands-on experience as a senior or principal-level practitioner in the gen AI era Real training in statistics, experimentation, or applied research you know how to design an evaluation that actually tests what you think it tests, not just one that looks reasonable Proven track record architecting and personally building enterprise gen AI systems in production with measurable customer impact Experience with consumer-facing or B2B customer-facing AI products — systems that real external users or customers depend on, not only internal tooling Builder at heart: still writes code, runs experiments, ships, and tunes prompts and evals, and wants to keep doing so as a leader Deep expertise across the modern gen AI stack: LLMs, agents, RAG, vector databases, embeddings, search, and evaluation harnesses Hands-on experience designing system-of-systems AI pipelines spanning search, retrieval, agent harnesses, and model selection/triage Strong proficiency with the Microsoft AI stack: Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Search, and supporting Azure infrastructure Excellent technical leadership skills; demonstrated ability to influence architecture and methodology decisions across product, engineering, and data science Strong communication skills, including explaining evaluation results and architecture trade-offs to executive and customer audiences Career experience spanning both a larger, established technology company and a smaller company or startup — comfortable operating with both institutional rigor and startup pace Mentor team members and contribute to a culture of continuous improvement Nice to Have (Preferred) Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in Statistics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field Peer-reviewed publications, technical writing, conference talks, or other evidence of contributing to the field, not just building within it Background building agentic systems with tool use, planning, and multi-step reasoning in production Prior experience setting up AI governance and evaluation harnesses in a regulated or high-stakes domain Open-source contributions or other evidence of being a recognized builder in the AI community A demonstrated track record of sticking with hard, ambiguous problems over long timeframes rather than pivoting away when the first approach doesn't work. title: Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior. The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD) About Sezzle : With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! Compensation : For this senior role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD based on experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work. About the Role: We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through. This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with. At Sezzle , AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own. What You’ll Do: Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones. Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it. Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering. Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery. Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt. Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations. Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own. Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own. What We Look For: 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience. Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days. Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python. Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure. Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus. Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring. Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate. Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted. Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build. Preferred Knowledge and Skills: Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope. Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence. Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA). Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer. Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right. Experience with threat modeling at a system level. About You: You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better. You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. Sezzle ’s Technology Stack: Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native Backend: Golang Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes Version Control: Git CI/CD: Gitlab Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying! What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome? At Sezzle , we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. #Li-remote #Full-time Originally posted on Himalayas

description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Mid-level. Overview Find the problem. Decide what to build. Ship it to production and prove it worked. Reporting to the CTO. Company Details Periskope helps businesses run customer conversations and operations on WhatsApp. Chats, groups, ticketing and automation live in one workspace, used by teams around the world. $2.5M+ ARR ~12 People Profitable · Global customers Seed · Saison Capital and Alliance Requirements 2–5 years: In engineering, product, a founder's office, or your own startup. Product intuition: You can look at a screen and say what is wrong with it, and why. Proof you build: Something real you made with AI tools. A product, an internal tool, an automation people still use. Hustle: You unblock yourself. You do not wait for a spec, a designer or permission. Appetite for depth: You do not need to know production systems today. You need to want to own them. Clear communication: You explain decisions, flag uncertainty early, and move work forward in a remote team. Responsibilities Customer problems: Talk to users every week. Turn what you hear into a clear call on what to build next. Concept to production: Scope it, build it with agents, deploy it, and iterate on real usage. A product surface: Own a part of Periskope end to end, and the metric it moves. What ships: Challenge agent output, test assumptions, and stay accountable for the code and the result. Production reliability: When something breaks, find out why and fix it. Learn the data models, APIs and WhatsApp infrastructure underneath. Job Details Remote for candidates based in India. Interview Process Share your profile and one thing you took from idea to shipped: the problem, what you built, how you used agents, and what changed. Shortlisted candidates move through three steps. Conversation · Async on WhatsApp Talk through your work and product decisions with Bharat (CTO). Build together · 90 minutes Take a real Periskope problem from brief to working build, live with Bharat. Final conversation · 20 minutes Discuss the role and mutual fit with Swapnika (CEO). Why This Role Exists For years, building software needed two people. A PM decided what to build. An engineer wrote the code. Most of the time went into the handoff between them. That split no longer makes sense. AI agents now write most of our code. Typing code stopped being the bottleneck. Judgment took its place: knowing which problem matters, what the smallest useful fix is, and whether it holds up in production. A Product Engineer is one person doing the whole loop. You talk to the customer, make the call, direct the agents, ship the change and watch what happens next. How the Work Flows Listen: Sales calls, support chats, churn reasons, usage data. Decide: Pick the problem that matters. Cut it to the smallest useful fix. Build: Direct agents. Review every diff. Test what they assume. Ship: Release to real customers, behind a flag if it is risky. Measure: Check usage and tickets. Keep it, fix it or kill it. Then back to listening. A good loop takes days, not quarters. Who This Is For You do not need an engineering title. You need taste, speed, and a real wish to build things that run in production. Engineers: Who care more about the customer than the stack. AR teams spend 60–70% of their week on manual follow-up instead of posting cash, closing disputes, or analyzing aging. Adding headcount doesn't fix it; manual follow-up simply doesn't scale, and every ERP hits the same wall. Problem and solution validation are complete. The teams that ship credible AI workers into finance-sensitive functions in the next 18 months will define the category. We intend to be one of them. The Venture Argentl delivers an AI collections agent that handles outbound debtor follow-up automatically — trained, monitored, and continuously improved by our team. Give us a list of overdue accounts and our voice agent calls each debtor, confirms invoice awareness, and captures exactly what they say — a payment commitment, a dispute, a request to split, or silence. The AR team gets a clean morning report: who's committed, who's disputing, who's gone silent, and what to do next. No ERP migration, no system credentials, no workflow overhaul — we're calling within a week of receiving the data. The roadmap expands from collections follow-up into adjacent AI finance-ops roles, all delivered through the same managed model. The Partnership The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, and live pilots are running. What remains is to bring on the technical co-founder — a partner who will own product and engineering with the same conviction, urgency, and ownership stake. This is a co-founder role, not a CTO hire. In return for that level of commitment, you receive founder-level equity, founder-level authority with co-decision rights on product, technology, hiring, fundraising, and strategy, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision. What you'll own As Co-Founder & CTO, you will take over the production code and continue building the product (the first lines of production code), set the technical direction, and lead execution end-to-end. Establish core architecture, observability, and audit-trail standards for a product that speaks to customers' debtors on their behalf. Mature the workflow engine so every call, intent classification, and next-action flows through reliably. title: Principal Harness Engineer
description: Employment type: Full Time. Seniority: Senior. FICO (NYSE: FICO ) is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential! The Opportunity Come join our engineering team in a hands-on technical role at the heart of a new discipline: Harness Engineering. As AI coding agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness). As a Senior Harness Engineer you'll independently own whole harness subsystems, set the standards other engineers build to, and be involved in the end-to-end lifecycle of turning raw model capability into production-grade engineering. What You’ll Contribute Design, build, deploy, and support core components of the harness - the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role focused on systems and leverage, not hand-writing application code. Own and evolve feedforward guides - agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods - and drive team-wide standardisation so agents get it right the first time. Build feedback sensors - custom linters, static analysis, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers. Own quality gating and release criteria for agent-produced work, defining authority boundaries for what agents may merge unaided and the escalation rules for what must route to a human. Establish LLM testing infrastructure and evaluation approaches that ensure AI-generated output meets quality and safety thresholds; apply consumer/contract testing (e.g. Pact) where service integration reliability matters. Run the steering loop - when an agent repeats a mistake, engineer a control so it can't happen again - and treat repository knowledge (docs, specs, context) as the system of record, fighting drift with continuous garbage collection. Decide where each control runs in the path to production - fast checks pre-commit, more expensive checks post-integration, and continuous sensors that scan for drift outside the change lifecycle - keeping quality as far left as is economical. Improve observability into agent work and track the measures that matter - cost per merged PR, time-to-merge for agent-assisted PRs, review velocity relative to PR size, defect escape rate, and agent-PR survival rate - using them to decide where to invest next. Partner with product and platform teams to turn specifications and acceptance criteria into enforceable controls. Serve as a source of technical expertise and mentor engineers across teams in harness practices and the effective, responsible use of AI tools. What We’re Seeking Bachelor's/Master's in Computer Science or related disciplines, or relevant commercial experience in software architecture, design, development, and testing. Seasoned software engineer with experience in large, complex codebases and a strong foundation in architecture and design; you care deeply about testing and maintainability. Hands-on experience with AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, or similar) and a well-developed feel for where they succeed and fail. Proven ability to build engineering tooling across a modern stack - linters and static analysis, CI/CD pipelines, containerised build/test environments, and instrumentation/observability - plus familiarity with agent instruction conventions such as AGENTS.md. Experience with spec-driven development, context engineering, agent orchestration, fitness functions, and developer-platform work. A systems mindset - you'd rather fix the environment than fix one output - and the ability to encode "what good looks like" into mechanical, repeatable rules. Judgement about when to reach for deterministic, computational controls (type checkers, linters, structural/architecture-fitness tests) versus inferential, LLM-based ones (AI code review, LLM-as-judge) - and an understanding of the cost, speed, and reliability trade-offs between them. Experience owning quality-gating processes and defining release criteria to ensure engineering standards are consistently met. Working knowledge of the security surface unique to autonomous agents - prompt injection, tool/permission scoping, sandboxed execution, and audit trails for agent actions - and how to design least-privilege guardrails around them. Experience with consumer/contract testing approaches (e.g. Pact) to validate service integrations across distributed systems. Excellent communication skills; able to articulate design with architects and drive standards across teams. Our Offer to You An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others. The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences. Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so. An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie. Why Make a Move to FICO ? At FICO , you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. You’ll play a part in our commitment to help businesses use data to improve every choice they make, using advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, and much more. FICO makes a real difference in the way businesses operate worldwide: • Credit Scoring — FICO ® Scores are used by 90 of the top 100 US lenders. • Fraud Detection and Security — 4 billion payment cards globally are protected by FICO fraud systems. • Lending — 3/4 of US mortgages are approved using the FICO Score. Global trends toward digital transformation have created tremendous demand for FICO ’s solutions, placing us among the world’s top 100 software companies by revenue. We help many of the world’s largest banks, insurers, retailers, telecommunications providers and other firms reach a new level of success. Our success is dependent on really talented people – just like you – who thrive on the collaboration and innovation that’s nurtured by a diverse and inclusive environment. We’ll provide the support you need, while ensuring you have the freedom to develop your skills and grow your career. Join FICO and help change the way business thinks! Learn more about how you can fulfil your potential at FICO promotes a culture of inclusion and seeks to attract a diverse set of candidates for each job opportunity. We are an equal employment opportunity employer and we’re proud to offer employment and advancement opportunities to all candidates without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. Research has shown that women and candidates from underrepresented communities may not apply for an opportunity if they don’t meet all stated qualifications. If you believe you have many, but not necessarily all, of the stated qualifications we encourage you to apply. Tool integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and familiarity with the EU AI Act. description: Employment type: Contractor. Seniority: Senior. About OpenMined OpenMined is a 501(c)(3) non-profit foundation that brings together leading minds in AI, security, and privacy technology to develop open-source solutions that transform how data can be accessed and shared. Founded in 2017, we've grown into a global community of over 18,000 members working to ensure that privacy protection and AI innovation reinforce each other rather than undermine one another. We are driven by a simple challenge: the most valuable data for solving humanity's greatest challenges remains locked away due to privacy concerns, and we can change that through technology rather than compromise. About the Role We're looking for a Senior / Staff Software Engineer to join OpenMined , a nonprofit building open-source infrastructure for federated AI. You’ll lead our 😱 ScreamingFace squad, the team that makes this vision real by building the internet's first leaderboard for fusion models (ensembles) and the open toolkit supporting benchmark evaluations for fusion models. Today, claims that the newest solo LLM beats the others are everywhere, and almost none of them can be checked or compared with the performance achieved by combining LLMs into more powerful fusion models. Results are self-reported, expensive to rerun, and hard to pick apart. We think there’s a better standard: every fusion and benchmark run compiles to a single line of text that anyone can replay for almost nothing, and a score counts only once someone else can reproduce it. The ScreamingFace toolkit is the open-source Python library and engine, leveraging our URL4 protocol, to let any researcher (a frontier lab, a university group, an independent builder) compose ensembles and routers across open and closed models, using their own keys, and grade them against pinned benchmarks. The ScreamingFace leaderboard is the public map of the quality–cost frontier, backed by a shared cache that makes every result on it cheap to verify and easy to build on. This is a hands-on technical leadership role . You understand the long term vision. You write code. You make architecture decisions. You set engineering standards by example. You're the most experienced engineer on the squad, the person others look to for production-quality judgment, and the voice that connects this team's decisions with the organization's broader platform strategy. The squad is talented and mission-driven and looking to strengthen its ability to continuously ship production software. You bring this production muscle: the instinct for what scales, the judgment about what to build and what to kill, and the craft to raise the team's standard through code review, pairing, and architectural guidance rather than mandates. If you're motivated by building distributed systems that matter, mentoring brilliant people who are just getting started, and making hard technical calls in a fast-moving nonprofit that's trying to change how the world shares data — we'd love to hear from you. You'll work most closely with Kevin McDonough, Head of Engineering. This is an independent contractor engagement, roughly a full-time commitment, with an initial 12-month term we expect to renew. You set your own schedule, but we need your working hours to overlap substantially with US Eastern business hours (your local time between one hour behind and two hours ahead of ET). Responsibilities Own the ScreamingFace squad technical architecture end to end — align design, engineering, and deployment across the stack to deliver reliable technical capabilities and user experience from current implementation through product roadmap evolution. Drive production readiness through deployment monitoring, error handling, graceful degradation, and operational runbooks. Be a force multiplier by establishing, demonstrating, and mentoring the team to establish norms around engineering best practices (including system design for modularity, security, reliability, & scalability), code quality, and delivery to production. Collaborate on core technology stack strategy through architectural review and identification of components that should become shared organizational primitives and defining standard interfaces that prevent tight coupling. Partner with product lead to develop and execute on realistic roadmaps that balance what is desired with what is feasible, scalable, and architecturally sound. Own the delivery of engineering’s quarterly goals, ensuring consistent, high-impact delivery while effectively managing resources. Own team output, delivery, and success (productivity, timeliness, morale) through appropriately matching team members and work to properly balance interest, learning opportunities, capacity, and capability. Champion high-quality software delivery through the establishment of robust tools, processes, & methodologies, and by providing hands-on technical leadership via individual development contributions and code reviews. Create technical documentation and processes that support high velocity and knowledge transfer. Actual offers will be determined based on the candidate's skills, level of experience, and location. About the role Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. Contract to cash Own ARR and bookings logic (new, upsell, downsell, churn, renewals) and keep agreement, opportunity, and invoice consistent. Run the closed-deals and billing check with Finance. Revenue analytics and data model Own the quarterly sales analytics pack, the CRO report, the forecast and pipeline coverage (including CS renewal inputs). Track funnel conversion, explain why deals move, stall or slip, and keep attribution correct with Marketing. Query ClickHouse daily, trace any number to its source, and write specs for model changes. Give each metric one documented definition and add data quality checks. Build leadership dashboards, retire unused ones, and end every analysis with a recommendation, a number and an owner. AI and automation Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for queries, scripts and Salesforce automation, and always verify their output. Automate manual work (invoice and payment checks, CRM hygiene, deal-risk alerts, call analysis) and measure hours saved and errors avoided. Ownership Be the single RevOps contact for Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance and Product. Turn each request into a task with an owner, date and success metric. Requirements 4-6+ years in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM systems in B2B SaaS, with hands-on admin of a live Salesforce org. Strong SQL and comfort in a modeled warehouse (layers, lineage, one definition per metric). dbt is a plus. Deep knowledge of the B2B SaaS revenue cycle: funnel, pipeline, forecast, ARR, churn, renewals. Experience running the money side: contracts, invoicing, collections, kept in sync with the CRM. Proof you build with AI agents: something you shipped that others use. Fluent English and clear written updates without being asked. Nice to have Salesforce Administrator or Advanced Administrator certification. ClickHouse or another columnar warehouse, and any BI tool. Salesforce development (Apex, triggers, API). Gong, Clay, Lemlist, or workflow automation tools. Billing, CPQ, or accounting systems. HubSpot to Salesforce migration. Attribution or CS health score data. Martech or analytics company background.
